title: Model onboarding requirements: compatibility matrix, version-pinning UX, and ingestion checklist
creator: Mariana Lopez
description:
Purpose: Define concrete product and engineering acceptance criteria for onboarding new open-source model artifacts into the Redwood Model Catalog. Scope includes: metadata schema, compatibility matrix (tokenizer/runtime/quantization), explicit version-pinning UX, ingestion validation checks (hash/signature), and rollout constraints for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Out of scope for this ticket: model quality vetting (evals) and commercial licensing negotiations. This ticket focuses on engineering and UX requirements necessary to safely surface models to customers and allow deterministic pinning semantics when customers choose a version.

Goals: 1) Ensure every catalog entry has machine-readable compatibility metadata for runtime selection and fallback. 2) Provide customers a clear pinning affordance that prevents silent minor-version drift. 3) Prevent common runtime incompatibilities at onboarding time (e.g., tokenizer mismatch, incompatible kv-cache format, unsupported quantization). 4) Make onboarding process auditable for Private/VPC installs (audit logs, checksum/signature verification).
acceptance_criteria: Catalog metadata schema is defined and implemented in the backend: fields include model_id, model_version, architecture, tokenizer_id, max_sequence_length, kv_cache_format, supported_quantizations (list), recommended_runtime_profiles (list), min_runtime_version, and suggested_batching_profile.

UI: Model detail page displays compatibility matrix (tokenizer, max_seq, quantizations supported, recommended runtime versions) and a clear "Pin this version" CTA. Pinning modal explains behavior: pinned deployments will continue to use exact model_version until unpinned or explicitly upgraded.

Onboarding validation: ingestion pipeline rejects artifacts with missing tokenizer mapping, unknown kv_cache_format, or mismatched architecture-tokenizer pairs and emits actionable errors in the catalog ingestion logs.

Version-pinning enforcement: when a deployment selects a pinned model_version, the routing layer will never route to a different model_version for that deployment; edge and Dedicated routing components have tests demonstrating pinned vs unpinned behavior.

Rollback & fallback policy: define and document automatic fallback behavior when a pinned model_version becomes unavailable (manual admin override required; optional auto-fallback to a compatible unpinned variant only after explicit customer opt-in).

Security/audit: ingestion includes checksum verification and records artifact provenance (uploader, timestamp, source URI) in audit logs visible in Private installs; onboarding requires security-team signoff flag for models marked "enterprise-sensitive".

E2E tests: automated ingestion + deploy playbook runs in CI: ingest sample open-model artifact (quantized and fp16 variants), create a pinned deployment, run generation and embedding sanity checks, and assert identical outputs for repeated runs across 3 seeds within tolerance thresholds.
Docs: engineering runbook and catalog onboarding guide published in Confluence with example CLI commands and a checklist for open-model contributors.
notes: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting — aligned PM, Runtime, Ingestion, and Console teams. Action: ENG to propose metadata schema by 2026-03-05 (ENG-3983).

2026-03-04: Trade-off discussed: strict vs permissive pinning. Decision: default to strict pinning for customer deployments, offer an opt-in automatic minor-version update flag for non-critical dev environments.
2026-03-05: Security requested artifact signature requirement for Private installs; added to acceptance criteria and security_review_required=true.
2026-03-07: UX mock reviewed — new Pin modal will include a 'why pin' tooltip, and show consequences for auto-updates; mock PR created (DES-4202).

2026-03-08: ENG raised a compatibility edge-case: some community builds change tokenizer bytes without bumping model_version. Added explicit ingestion check for tokenizer hash mismatch and a recommended remediation step.
